label: Boogu Image
promptingNotes: Reads natural language through a Qwen3-VL text encoder: write full, specific sentences, subject first, then setting, lighting, composition and style. Long, detailed prompts work well; tag lists and quality tags such as "masterpiece, best quality" add little. Put any text to render in the image in quotes. The seeded defaults are the Turbo checkpoint's — 3 to 4 steps at CFG 1. The Base checkpoint wants 25 to 50 steps at CFG 2 to 5 (4 is the vendor's example), and renders at 1K, 1.5K and 2K.

label: Boogu Image Edit
promptingNotes: An instruction editor: attach one reference image — it takes one for now — and say in plain words what to change ("change 'flux.cpp' to 'boogu.cpp'"), naming what must stay as it is. It inserts, replaces and removes objects, changes attributes, materials and backgrounds, and keeps the source subject and composition coherent. The reference is read by Qwen3-VL-8B, which is why this architecture also loads its vision projector. The seeded defaults are Edit Turbo's — 4 steps at CFG 1, so the negative prompt has no effect. The full Edit checkpoint wants 25 to 50 steps at CFG 2 to 5 (5 is the vendor's example). It renders up to 2K, and is most stable at 1K.

label: ERNIE Image
promptingNotes: Reads natural language through a Ministral 3B text encoder: write full, specific sentences, subject first, then setting, lighting, composition and style. Long, detailed prompts work well; tag lists and quality tags such as "masterpiece, best quality" add little. Put any text to render in the image in quotes. The seeded defaults are the Turbo checkpoint's — 8 steps at CFG 1. The full checkpoint wants 50 steps at CFG 4 to 5, and both were trained on 1024x1024, 848x1264, 1264x848, 768x1376, 896x1200, 1376x768 and 1200x896.

label: Flux.2 Klein 9B
promptingNotes: Reads natural language through an LLM text encoder: write full, specific sentences, subject first, then setting, lighting, composition and style. label: HiDream O1 Image
promptingNotes: Reads natural language: write full, specific sentences, subject first, then setting, lighting, composition and style. Long, detailed prompts work well; tag lists and quality tags such as "masterpiece, best quality" add little. Put any text to render in the image in quotes. The seeded defaults are the Dev checkpoint's — 28 steps, no CFG, flow shift 1. The full checkpoint wants 50 steps at CFG 5 with flow shift 3. It was trained around 2048x2048 (2048x2048, 2304x1728, 2560x1440, 2496x1664, 3104x1312, 2304x1792 and their portraits); at 1024 it loses detail. Sides are multiples of 32. One file holds the whole model: no separate VAE or text encoder, only its tokenizer.json. On the drift runner each checkpoint samples as the vendor's does — the Dev one over its distilled timesteps with fresh noise each step, the full one with UniPC — where sd-cpp runs plain Euler, which leaves the Dev images looking unfinished. On the drift runner the same checkpoints also edit and compose: attach one or more reference images and say in plain words what to change or how to combine them, naming what must stay as it is. References are read through Qwen3-VL-8B's vision projector, in the optional slot; a prompt alone does not need it.

label: Ideogram 4
promptingNotes: Trained only on structured JSON captions: the prompt is one JSON object, not prose, and key ORDER matters. "high_level_description" (one or two sentences: shot, subject, setting); "style_description" with, in this order, "aesthetics", "lighting", then exactly one of "photo" (camera and lens, medium "photograph") or "medium" + "art_style" (illustration, painting, 3d_render…), optional "color_palette" last (uppercase #RRGGBB, up to 16); "compositional_deconstruction" (required) with "background" then "elements": {"type":"obj","bbox":[y_min,x_min,y_max,x_max] on 0–1000 (optional),"desc":…} or {"type":"text","bbox":…,"text":"literal text","desc":…}. Describe everything visible, exhaustively. Real classifier-free guidance through the second, unconditional model: CFG 7 and 20 steps by default (48 for quality); the negative prompt is ignored. Any multiple-of-16 size from 256 to 2048 per side.

label: Krea 2
promptingNotes: Reads natural language through an LLM text encoder: write full, specific sentences, subject first, then setting, lighting, composition and style. Long, detailed prompts work well; tag lists and quality tags such as "masterpiece, best quality" add little. Put any text to render in the image in quotes.

label: Mage-Flow
promptingNotes: Reads natural language through Qwen3-VL-4B: write full sentences, subject first, then setting, lighting, composition and style, and put any text to render in the image in quotes. Three checkpoints share these slots and each carries its own numbers: the RL-aligned one (mage_flow) 20 steps at CFG 5, Base (mage_flow_base) 30 steps at CFG 5, Turbo (mage_flow_turbo) 4 steps at CFG 1. With guidance on, the negative prompt counts and each step costs two passes; at Turbo's CFG 1 it has no effect. A checkpoint registered without parameters gets the RL-aligned one's. Width and height must be multiples of 16; trained at native resolutions from 512 to 2048 per side.

label: Mage-Flow Edit
promptingNotes: An instruction editor: attach one or more reference images and say in plain words what to change ("change 'flux.cpp' to 'mage.cpp'"), naming what must stay as it is. Each reference is read by Qwen3-VL-4B (longest edge capped at 384 px) and fed to the transformer at the output size, so keep the output's aspect ratio that of the reference. Three checkpoints share these slots and each carries its own numbers: RL-aligned (mage_flow_edit) and Base (mage_flow_edit_base) 30 steps at CFG 5, Turbo (mage_flow_edit_turbo) 4 steps at CFG 1. With guidance on, the negative prompt counts and each step costs two passes; at Turbo's CFG 1 it has no effect. A checkpoint registered without parameters gets 30 steps at CFG 5. On sd-cpp it runs without flash attention: with it, on ROCm, sd-cpp draws squiggles all over the edit. Width and height must be multiples of 16, 512 to 2048 per side.

label: LLaDA-Image Turbo
promptingNotes: A 6B image and editing model, distilled to 4 steps at CFG 1, so the negative prompt has no effect. Reads natural language, English or Chinese, through the LLaDA2 language model: write a plain description, and put any text to render in the image in quotes. The same checkpoint edits: attach one reference image and say what to change; the SigVQ slot (optional) is what reads the reference, so editing needs it. The base and Turbo files are not interchangeable: keep each model's transformer, text encoder, QueryFormer and text projection together. Width and height must be multiples of 32. It runs on the drift runner only, from the official files.

label: LLaDA-Image
promptingNotes: A 6B image and editing model, the base one: 50 steps at CFG 5, where the negative prompt has an effect; edit at 1024x1024 (at 512 it tends to give the reference back). Reads natural language, English or Chinese, through the LLaDA2 language model: write a plain description, and put any text to render in the image in quotes. The same checkpoint edits: attach one reference image and say what to change; the SigVQ slot (optional) is what reads the reference, so editing needs it. The base and Turbo files are not interchangeable: keep each model's transformer, text encoder, QueryFormer and text projection together. Width and height must be multiples of 32. It runs on the drift runner only, from the official files.

label: GRN
promptingNotes: An experimental model that does not diffuse: a picture is a grid of bits, all predicted again at each of 50 steps while a growing share of them is kept. Text to image only, 2B parameters; CFG 3 is the vendor's setting and the negative prompt has an effect. Write a plain description through umT5 (the Wan text encoder, as a safetensors file: the runner does not read its GGUF). Trained around a megapixel; width and height must be multiples of 16. Its weights are published as PyTorch pickles, which drift does not read: the built-in files are a safetensors conversion of the official ones (drift-generator/grn-safetensor). It runs on the drift runner only.

label: Nucleus-Image
promptingNotes: A base model (17B parameters, a mixture of experts of which about 2B run per step), not distilled: 50 steps at CFG 4 are the vendor's settings, and the negative prompt has an effect. Reads natural language through Qwen3-VL-8B and follows it literally: say where things are (left, right), how many, and which colour goes with which object. Put any text to render in the image in quotes. Trained at about a megapixel: 1024x1024, 1344x768, 1184x896, 1248x832 and their portraits. Width and height must be multiples of 16. It runs on the drift runner only: sd-cpp does not know the model.

label: Qwen Image
promptingNotes: Reads natural language through an LLM text encoder: write full, specific sentences, subject first, then setting, lighting, composition and style. Long, detailed prompts work well; tag lists and quality tags such as "masterpiece, best quality" add little. Put any text to render in the image in quotes. It is especially strong at rendering text, Chinese included.

label: Qwen Image 2.1
promptingNotes: Reads natural language through Qwen3-VL-8B: write full, specific sentences, subject first, then setting, lighting, composition and style. Long, detailed prompts work well; tag lists and quality tags such as "masterpiece, best quality" add little. Put any text to render in the image in quotes — it is especially strong at text, Chinese included. Its own pipeline runs 40 euler steps without guidance, and so do drift's defaults: CFG 1, where the negative prompt is not read. A CFG above 1 turns on real classifier-free guidance, the negative prompt with it, at twice the time a step; 2 to 3 stays clean; from about 4 up the picture reddens and smooths, and at 6 (sd-cpp's example) it is over-saturated, smeared and carries a faint 8-pixel pattern. A turbo LoRA brings the steps down to 4 to 6. The same checkpoint edits: attach one or more reference images and say in plain words what to change ("change 'qwen2.1.cpp' to 'sd.cpp'"), naming what must stay as it is. Editing reads the references through the text encoder, so it needs the Qwen3-VL-8B vision projector in the optional slot; generating from a prompt alone does not.

label: SenseNova U1.5
promptingNotes: A unified model that denoises in pixel space and reads the prompt with its own language model (the SenseNova prompt template is applied automatically): describe the scene in full sentences, subject first. Official settings: 50 Euler steps, CFG 4, flow shift 3, empty negative prompt. Width and height must be multiples of 32; the 1:1 training size is 2048×2048, smaller sizes fall outside its training buckets. Text-to-image only: editing and thinking-mode prompt expansion are not implemented in sd-cpp.

label: Z-Image Turbo
promptingNotes: Reads natural language through an LLM text encoder: write full, specific sentences, subject first, then setting, lighting, composition and style. Long, detailed prompts work well; tag lists and quality tags such as "masterpiece, best quality" add little. Put any text to render in the image in quotes. It renders text well, in English and Chinese.

label: HunyuanVideo 1.5
promptingNotes: A video model reading natural language through Qwen2.5-VL 7B, in English or Chinese: describe the subject and what it does, the scene, then the camera and how it moves. Text to show in the video goes in quotes; a ByT5 glyph encoder renders it. Match the size to the checkpoint: 1280×720 for the 720p ones, 848×480 for the 480p ones. Frame counts of the form 4n+1 (33 by default).

label: LTX 2.3
promptingNotes: A video model reading natural language: describe the scene and subject, then what moves and how over the clip, then the camera (static, pan, dolly, orbit). One continuous shot, concrete actions rather than moods.

label: SeedVR2 upscaler
promptingNotes: An upscaler for pictures and videos: it takes no prompt. It restores in one diffusion step and redraws fine detail, so faces and textures can change.

label: FLUX 3 Image Klein
promptingNotes: Trained on the long captions of its own prompt upsampler, and noticeably weaker on a short prompt sent as typed: write one continuous prose description of 100 to 350 words, medium and style first ("Full-color outdoor photograph, ..."), then the scene, lighting and camera, then each subject with its colours, materials and place in the frame (frame-left, foreground, ...). Every person gets an observable profile; text to render goes in double quotes, verbatim. No quality tags, no mood words. Edits with up to 10 reference images, one at the output's size edited in place. The distilled checkpoint runs 16 steps without CFG, the base one 50 steps at CFG 4.
